Phase 2. Design and implement based on the Gherkin specification.

---

## Context-dependent behaviour

| Context | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| First cycle | Full design and implementation |
| Later cycles | Reflect the design of affected parts and fix the implementation |

---

## Implementation basis

Use the GWT (Gherkin) of approved scenarios as the basis for functional behaviour.
Do not arbitrarily add behaviour not included in the Gherkin.
Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
scenarios' GWT specifications. Develop the production code in `implementation/`,
separately from the exploration code in `prototypes/`.

This restriction applies to exploration code, including prototypes made in later
cycles. Later cycles may modify the existing production implementation according
to the updated approved GWT; they do not require rebuilding it from scratch.

---

## Internal information system

Accumulate the following information during implementation. Keep the format
lightweight, but at a level that enables impact analysis in later cycles.

### Design-decision record
What was decided, why, and which alternatives were dropped.
Notes for understanding the structure after context is reset.

### Scenario-code mapping
Which scenario (SCN-NNN) corresponds to which code.
The basis for judging the impact scope on a change request.

### Tests
Create tests together with the implementation.
Include both Gherkin-based acceptance tests and internal unit/integration tests.

---

## Sufficiency criteria

The internal information system is sufficient when it meets both of:
- A level that enables impact analysis in later cycles
- A level from which, if the user requests traditional artifacts (design
  documents, test plans, etc.), they can be generated and provided

---

## Transition to Phase 3

When implementation and test creation are complete, switch to Phase 3
(verification).

Title: Save a recognizable bookmark from a page address
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

From an empty personal bookmark library, the client pastes a page address into a clear address box at the top and saves it. The saved bookmark appears in the library with the page's real title, a plain-language description, and the website name, making it recognizable without opening the page.

## Gherkin

Feature: Save bookmarks

  Scenario: Save a link with recognizable page details
    Given the personal bookmark library is empty
    And a clear address box for saving a bookmark is shown at the top
    When the user enters a page address and saves the bookmark
    Then the bookmark appears in the library
    And it shows the page title
    And it shows a plain-language page description
    And it shows the website name

## Assumptions

- Saving a bookmark begins from a prominent address box at the top of the library.
- The app obtains page details automatically after the user supplies the address.
- A bookmark's recognizable summary consists of its title, description, and website name.

## Related scenarios

- None
Scenario ID: SCN-002
Title: Correct a bookmark's recognizable details inline
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-002
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

From a saved bookmark, the client chooses Edit details and corrects the title or description directly within that bookmark. Saving the changes returns the bookmark to its usual display with the correction in place and a brief confirmation that it was updated.

## Gherkin

Feature: Correct bookmark details

  Scenario: Correct a bookmark title or description inline
    Given a saved bookmark shows its title and description
    When the user chooses to edit its details
    Then editable title and description fields appear inline within that bookmark
    When the user changes the title or description and saves the changes
    Then the bookmark returns to its usual display
    And it shows the corrected title and description
    And a brief update confirmation is shown

## Assumptions

- Editing begins from an Edit details control on the bookmark.
- Quick correction includes the title and description, but not the website name or page address.
- The selected interaction is inline editing rather than a modal or side drawer.
- Changing the saved page address is recorded as a request for a later cycle.

Scenario ID: SCN-003
Title: Reuse an existing tag through typing suggestions
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-003
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

From a saved bookmark, the client chooses Add tag beneath the bookmark and begins typing. Matching tags used before are suggested inline and identified as existing tags. Choosing a suggestion adds that existing tag beneath the bookmark and briefly confirms the update, avoiding an accidental duplicate tag.

## Gherkin

Feature: Organize bookmarks with consistent tags

  Scenario: Add a previously used tag to a bookmark
    Given a saved bookmark does not have the existing tag "Recipes"
    And "Recipes" has been used on another bookmark before
    When the user chooses Add tag beneath the bookmark
    And types text matching "Recipes"
    Then "Recipes" is suggested as a tag used before
    When the user chooses the "Recipes" suggestion
    Then the existing "Recipes" tag appears beneath the bookmark
    And a brief confirmation is shown
    And no duplicate tag is created

## Assumptions

- Tags appear beneath each bookmark.
- Adding a tag uses an inline type-to-find interaction.
- Matching existing tags are labeled as used before.
- Example existing tags during approval were Recipes, Research, and Design.

Scenario ID: SCN-004
Title: Browse bookmarks by a tag in the sidebar
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-004
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

The client's tags are visible at a glance in the sidebar with a count beside each one. Choosing "Recipes" narrows the library to bookmarks with that tag. The filtered view clearly identifies Recipes as the active tag and shows the number of matching bookmarks, reassuring the client that the filter took effect.

## Gherkin

Feature: Browse bookmarks by tag

  Scenario: Show bookmarks belonging to one tag
    Given the library contains two bookmarks tagged "Recipes"
    And it contains one bookmark without the "Recipes" tag
    And the sidebar lists tags with their bookmark counts
    When the user chooses "Recipes" in the sidebar
    Then only the two bookmarks tagged "Recipes" are shown
    And "Recipes" is identified as the active tag
    And the result count shows two bookmarks

## Assumptions

- The sidebar is the primary place for browsing tags.
- Each sidebar tag shows its bookmark count.
- The filtered result area shows both the active tag and matching bookmark count.

Title: Search bookmark titles, descriptions, and personal notes
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-005
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

The client searches from a prominent box above the library and results narrow live while typing. A query can find a bookmark through its title, description, or personal note. When a result matched only through a note, the bookmark explains that source and shows the relevant note text. The matching bookmark count is shown.

## Gherkin

Feature: Search bookmarks

  Scenario Outline: Search across recognizable bookmark text
    Given the library contains bookmarks with titles, descriptions, and personal notes
    When the user types a query found in a bookmark's <field>
    Then the results update live
    And only matching bookmarks are shown
    And the matching bookmark count is shown

    Examples:
      | field       |
      | title       |
      | description |
      | note        |

  Scenario: Explain a result matched only through a personal note
    Given the query does not appear in a bookmark's title or description
    And the query appears in that bookmark's personal note
    When the user types the query
    Then that bookmark is shown in the results
    And the result states that the match came from the user's note
    And it shows the relevant note text

## Assumptions

- Search updates live as the user types.
- The search box appears prominently above the bookmark library.
- Search is not limited to page addresses or exact address matching.

Scenario ID: SCN-006
Title: Complete a bookmark from the Read later list without deleting it
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-006
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

The client marks a bookmark using a clearly labeled Read later button. The button changes to show that the bookmark is in Read later, the sidebar count increases, and the bookmark remains in the main library. Choosing Read later in the sidebar opens a dedicated list with the waiting bookmark and count. Marking it as read removes it from that list and reduces the count without deleting it; returning to All bookmarks shows it alongside the other bookmarks, no longer flagged for later.

## Gherkin

Feature: Manage a Read later list

  Scenario: Mark a bookmark to read later
    Given a bookmark is in the main library and is not waiting to be read
    When the user chooses its labeled Read later action
    Then the action states that the bookmark is in Read later
    And the Read later sidebar count increases
    And the bookmark remains in the main library

  Scenario: Review bookmarks waiting to be read
    Given one bookmark is marked for later
    When the user chooses Read later in the sidebar
    Then the dedicated Read later view shows only that bookmark
    And it shows a count of one bookmark
    And the bookmark offers a Mark as read action

  Scenario: Mark a waiting bookmark as read without deleting it
    Given a bookmark is shown in the Read later view
    When the user marks it as read
    Then it is removed from the Read later view
    And the Read later sidebar count becomes zero
    And the view states that the bookmark remains in All bookmarks
    When the user returns to All bookmarks
    Then the bookmark is shown with the other bookmarks
    And it is no longer marked for later

## Assumptions

- Read later is always visible in the sidebar with its item count.
- The primary marking control is a clearly labeled button rather than an unlabeled icon or checkbox.
- Completing a Read later item clears its waiting flag and never deletes the bookmark.

    Given a saved bookmark has an original page address
    When the user clicks the bookmark card
    Then the original page opens in a new browser tab

Scenario ID: SCN-008
Title: Recover cleanly from bookmark saving problems
Type: Error Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-008
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

Saving handles three common problems without losing the client's work or cluttering the library. An incomplete address stays in the field with a plain inline explanation of a complete address. If page details cannot be retrieved, the valid address is kept and the client can supply a required title and optional description. If the page was already saved, the app warns the client and shows the existing bookmark instead of creating another copy.

## Gherkin

Feature: Recover from bookmark saving problems

  Scenario: Reject an incomplete page address without clearing it
    Given the user has entered text that is not a complete page address
    When the user tries to save it
    Then no bookmark is created
    And the entered text remains in the address field
    And an inline message explains that a complete address starts with http:// or https://

  Scenario: Save recognizable details when page details are unavailable
    Given the user has entered a valid page address
    And the app cannot retrieve its title and description
    When the retrieval attempt finishes
    Then the valid address is retained
    And the user is told that page details could not be retrieved
    And the user can provide a required title
    And the user can provide an optional description
    And the bookmark can be saved with those details

  Scenario: Avoid creating a duplicate bookmark
    Given a bookmark with the entered page address already exists
    When the user tries to save the same address again
    Then no duplicate bookmark is created
    And the user is told that the page is already saved
    And the existing bookmark is shown

## Assumptions

- A usable page address begins with http:// or https://.
- A manually supplied title is required for recognizability; a description is optional.
- Page addresses uniquely identify duplicate bookmarks in this cycle.

Scenario ID: SCN-009
Title: Deliberately create a new tag when no existing tag matches
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-009
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

When the client types a tag name and no existing tag matches, the inline suggestion clearly offers to create that tag rather than silently guessing. Choosing it creates and adds the tag in the same place. The first letter is tidied to uppercase for consistent presentation. Together with existing-tag suggestions, this lets the client deliberately grow the tag set without accidental duplicates.

## Gherkin

Feature: Add tags to bookmarks

  Scenario: Create and add a genuinely new tag
    Given a saved bookmark is ready to receive a tag
    And no existing tag matches the name the user types
    When the user types "travel" in the inline tag field
    Then an explicit "Travel — Create new tag" choice is shown
    When the user chooses that option
    Then a new tag named "Travel" is created
    And it is added beneath the bookmark
    And the user remains in the same context

## Assumptions

- Creating a tag is always an explicit choice, never a silent fallback.
- The first letter of a newly created tag is normalized to uppercase for display.
- Existing tag matching remains the preferred path when a match exists.

  Scenario: Show an understandable no-results state
    Given the library contains bookmarks
    When the user types a query that matches no title, description, or personal note
    Then no bookmark cards are shown
    And the query remains visible
    And the result count shows zero bookmarks
    And a message says that no bookmarks match the search

  Scenario: Clear an unsuccessful search
    Given a search has no matching bookmarks
    When the user clears the query using the control inside the search box
    Then the search box is empty
    And the full bookmark library returns immediately
    And the full bookmark count is restored

## Assumptions

- The clear-search control appears inside the search box while a query is present.
- Clearing a query does not require a separate submission action.

Title: Prevent a correction from leaving a bookmark without a title
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved

Title and description can be corrected inline and the description may be empty.   Scenario: Block an empty bookmark title
    Given a saved bookmark is being edited inline
    When the user erases its title
    And tries to save the changes
    Then the editor remains open
    And the title field is identified
    And a message explains that a title is needed for recognizability
    And the empty title is not saved

    And saves the changes

- Bookmark descriptions are optional.

Scenario ID: SCN-013
Title: Keep oversized bookmark cards scannable without hiding tags
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-013
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

A bookmark with a very long title, description, or note is compacted in the library so the list remains easy to scan. A Show full bookmark action expands the card to reveal all of its text. Tags are never hidden or cut off; all tags remain visible and wrap onto additional lines as needed.

## Gherkin

Feature: Display oversized bookmark content

  Scenario: Compact long text while keeping expansion available
    Given a bookmark has a very long title, description, or personal note
    When it is shown in the bookmark library
    Then its long text is compacted to keep the list scannable
    And a Show full bookmark action is available
    When the user chooses Show full bookmark
    Then the complete title, description, and note are shown

  Scenario: Keep all tags visible on an oversized bookmark
    Given a bookmark has more tags than fit on one line
    When it is shown in the bookmark library
    Then every tag remains visible
    And the tags wrap onto additional lines

## Assumptions

- Compaction applies to long title, description, and note text in library cards.
- Tags are recognition and finding aids and therefore are not compacted away.

Scenario ID: SCN-014
Title: Preserve saved information when the original website later fails
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-014
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

If an original website later changes or disappears, Keepwell retains the saved title, description, personal note, tags, and stored address without deleting or rewriting anything. Clicking the bookmark still tries the stored address in a new tab, even if the website itself then shows an error. Correcting the stored address is recorded for a later cycle.

## Gherkin

Feature: Preserve bookmarks independently of their source websites

  Scenario: Keep saved information after the original website becomes unavailable
    Given a bookmark has a saved title, description, personal note, tags, and page address
    And the original website later becomes unavailable
    When the bookmark is viewed in Keepwell
    Then all saved bookmark information remains unchanged
    And the bookmark is not deleted

  Scenario: Still attempt an unavailable original address
    Given the original website for a saved bookmark is unavailable
    When the user opens the bookmark card
    Then Keepwell attempts the stored address in a new tab
    And the website may show its own error
    And the saved bookmark remains unchanged

## Assumptions

- Keepwell does not automatically rewrite or delete saved information based on later source-website availability.
- Manual correction of a stored page address is a later-cycle request.

Phase 4. Present the result to the user and obtain acceptance confirmation.

---

## Acceptance procedure

### Presenting the result

Present the implemented software to the client and report that verification
against the approved scenarios' GWT specifications and the internal tests has
passed. Summarise the verification outcome in plain language and provide access
to the implemented software.

For the first cycle, the report covers all approved scenarios. For later cycles,
it covers the changed scenarios and affected existing scenarios.

### Acceptance confirmation

Ask the client to accept the implemented software as a whole on the basis of
the approved behaviour and the verification report. Acceptance completes the
development work for the cycle.

### Handling client requests

Use the requirement scenarios approved during Phase 1 as the baseline. Classify
each request by whether fulfilling it changes that baseline:

- Implementation error: the implementation does not satisfy an approved
  scenario. Return to Phase 2, fix the implementation, repeat verification in
  Phase 3, and request acceptance again. Preserve the approved scenario.
- Requirement change or addition: fulfilling the request requires changing an
  approved scenario or adding a scenario. Record the request for the next cycle
  in context/session-log.md, retaining the current approved scenarios.

Explain the classification using the previously approved behaviour in plain
language. If the client's request is unclear, clarify whether the software fails
to perform that behaviour or the desired behaviour has changed. Keep requirement
exploration within Phase 1 of the cycle that will address the change.

After recording a requirement change or addition, ask for acceptance of the
current software, for example:
"I've recorded that request for the next cycle. The software implements the
behaviour we approved, and its verification is complete. Do you accept this
software and agree to complete this cycle?"

Wait for the client's explicit acceptance. A request recorded for a later cycle
does not itself constitute acceptance of the current software.

---

## Transition to idle

When acceptance confirmation is complete, switch to the idle state. In this
experiment, the trial ends after acceptance of the first cycle. Retain requests
for later cycles in the session log.

---

## Session log

On acceptance completion, record the following in the session log:
- List of accepted scenarios
- Cycle number
- Acceptance result (approved / partially approved / rejected)
- Requirement changes or additions recorded for a later cycle
